title: The Finisher’s Clock: When Should Royal Challengers Bengaluru Send in Its Power Hitters?
dek: When should Royal Challengers Bengaluru send in their power hitters? The answer depends on how much a set batter is worth in the last five overs.
excerpt: Across the IPL since 2022, batters already set by the death overs out-score those who arrive late. That trade-off decides when Royal Challengers Bengaluru's finishers should walk out.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: A Clock, Not a Batting Order
body: Finishers are usually discussed as a position. In practice they are a timing decision: send the hitter in too early and he burns his innings against the middle-overs spinners, too late and he has three balls to change a match.

The league-wide evidence since 2022 shows what being set is worth. Batters who were already at the crease before the eleventh over struck at {{ev:fin-lset}} in the death overs; batters who arrived in the last five overs struck at {{ev:fin-lfresh}}.

sections.heading: Who Should Walk Out When
body: Since 2024, {{ev:finb-lead-name}} has led RCB in death-overs balls faced, with {{ev:finb-lead-balls}} at a strike rate of {{ev:finb-lead-sr}}.
The implication is a flexible order: when the platform is strong, the best hitter should walk out earlier than tradition says, so that he is set by the sixteenth over.

sections.heading: Selection Bias in the Numbers
body: Batters who are set by the death overs are often the better batters, which inflates their strike rate. Late arrivals include lower-order bowlers who would struggle at any point.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Send the Hitter Early Enough to Be Set
body: Royal Challengers Bengaluru should treat the finisher's entry as a clock. Because set batters out-score late arrivals in the death, the best hitter should be in by the twelfth or thirteenth over whenever wickets allow.
That changes how the batting order is written: as a set of triggers rather than fixed numbers.

seo.metaDescription: Set batters against late arrivals in the death overs, and what it means for when Royal Challengers Bengaluru's power hitters should walk out.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Run rates use all runs per legal ball times six. Every figure is generated from the CricField warehouse by scripts/editorial/engine. Arrival = the over of a batter's first ball faced. Death overs = sixteen to twenty. Bands with fewer than forty RCB balls are not shown for the team.
